Messages.Author: Owen P Reynolds
Messages.Body:
Rotschreck isn't a very good defensive card, I agree. The reason
for that is that it is a very powerfull offensive card which makes
Gangrel decks much more effective. If you have a Gangrel deck, stick
in a bunch of these cards.
    It can be played to advantage any time you are in a position to
use an aggravated damage strike for 1 point of damage. This would
usually be done with Claws of the Damned (or two of them to get to
close range vs. a gun-wielder. There's no limit on combat cards.)

o It effectively makes the victim lose a turn in addition to torpor.
o It prevents your vampire from taking any damage.
o It counters the effect of any and all defensive cards. This
  includes all Fortitude cards, Flak Vests, dodges and Majesty.
o It can be used on your turn.

    First some hand-waving about who it affects. From the card:

    "Play when a minion attempts to use aggravated damage against a
vampire... Combat ends before damage is resolved. That vampire is put
in torpor, tapped. ..."

    It shows a vampire cringing in fear from a sunny window. Now, from
Damn Operation we know that this is artistic license, since vampires
go abroad at night, but the card obviously involves fear. It isn't a
big stretch to say that the vampire about to take agravated damage
suddenly gets afraid and acts like the vampire in the picture. I guess
it runs away and becomes catatonic for a turn.
    To interpret this as affecting the vampire with the aggravated
damage weapon, you not only have to change the card in two places,
but have to invent a really strange rational for what happens.    

    Why I say it can do all those things:
#1. A point of aggravated damage sends the victim to torpor. This card
    send it to torpor and makes it stay tapped, so enchances a 1-point
    aggravated attack

#2. OK, it won't stop the Wolf Companion, but it goes before first
    strike or anything else.

#3. Since you have to play this card before damage is assigned, you
    won't so much as negate fortitude cards as you'll prevent someone
    from playing them.

    For Majesty, I read the rules carefully. Suppose the weasel you're
blocking plays Majesty. This card stops combat "before any damage is
dealt or any strike's effects take place." You still go ahead and choose
hands and play Claws of the Damned.
    Now you go to resolve strike. At this point you play Rotschreck
which also takes effect before damage is resolved. The two cases I can
see are that Rotschreck takes precedence, since it was played last, or
both take effect (allowing the vampire to pay a point of blood to
untap while in torpor.)
    Either way, Rotschreck lets you make one Majestic vampire pay
for trying to attack you.

#4. The card says when it can be used, which may occur during your turn.
    Even thought the rules say differently, this seems like a fairly
    clear case of a card overruling a rule. The card only says it can
    be used "when" the situation occurs and not "anytime" it happens,
    so the case could be stronger.

    My opinion is that there isn't a rule at all about using out-of-turn
    cards not on your turn, but that the rules are merely explaining how
    these work and most out-of-turn cards work that way.
--

Messages.Body:

> it can be. My oppinion is that "when a minion attempts to use
> aggravated damage against a vampire" is a sufficient description
> of when you use it that it can be used whenever that happens, on
> your turn or not.

Well...that would seem to make it pointless for a difference between 
action modifiers and reactions.  Many reaction cards say "only usable
during a political action", and if we are to use your logic for the
out-of-turn cards, then that follows for the reaction cards as well.
Forget the rules boys...play your cards whenever you want...regardless
of rules.

Oh, by the way...I assume that card text limitations are more like
sub-limitations, or additional limitations.  A reaction card must
follow both the "not on your turn" rule from the rule-book, and also
the "only during a political action" on the card.  An out-of-turn card
must follow the "not on your turn" from the rule-book, and any
additional conditions on the card, such as:
may be used when a minion attempts to use aggravated damage...

    First off, I'd like to be clear that my main point in even
posting on this thread is to get an explanation about why some
people think Rotschreck is played on a vampire _using_ aggravated
damage.
    I don't mind discussion my opinions about the "not on your
turn" pseudo-rule, but it's not what I really want to hear about.

>Oh, by the way...I assume that card text limitations are more like
>sub-limitations, or additional limitations.  A reaction card must
>follow both the "not on your turn" rule from the rule-book, and also
>the "only during a political action" on the card.  An out-of-turn card
>must follow the "not on your turn" from the rule-book, and any
>additional conditions on the card, such as:
>may be used when a minion attempts to use aggravated damage...

    I agree, but I think you're stretching the point. Dread Gaze and
Bewitching Oration are the exact same card except for the <> and <-
symbols on them, so it's obvious one is used by the acting minion only
and one is a reaction. The distinction between reaction and action
modifier is important for several cards.
    For out-of-turn cards, as I said before, the "not during your turn"
phrase, which I don't think even is a rule, but a not-completely
accurate remark, could easily be ignored and it wouldn't change
very much at all. It would make Brujah Frenzy a tiny bit more useful,
and make Rotschreck a decent card for a Gangrel deck (as opposed to
a way to maim any of your predator's minions you manage to block.)

    I've tried to post examples of how you can't play by the rules,
since read literally they make no sense, and now we've got the goofy
ruling about Wolf Companion (and I'm still right about Form of Mist
not working with action cards, even though I agree with Tom's
interpretation.)
    Just like it was explained that the phrase about _other_ Methuselahs
being able to use Pol ACt cards for votes was just plain written wrong,
I think the out-of-turn rules was just plain written wrong.
--

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Owen P Reynolds <owen@iastate.edu> wrote:
>>>o It can be used on your turn.
>>Master: out of turn.
>>Can't be played on your turn. (Unless of course that ruling has changed
>>but I haven't read it yet.)
>    Card text overrides rules. I hope we can all agree that an out-of-turn
>master can be played on your turn if it says it can be. My opinion is that
>"when a minion attempts to use aggravated damage against a vampire" is a
>sufficient description of when you use it that it can be used whenever
>that happens, on your turn or not.

Sorry, but wrong.  An out-of-turn card would only be usable during your
turn if it explicitly said it could be; assuming that it can be used during
your turn "because it makes sense" is reading something into the card
that isn't there.  Rotschreck is an out-of-turn card, and doesn't say it
can be used during your turn, so can't be used during your turn.

>    That's like saying that most cards starting with the letter 'R'
>aren't very useful, so Rotschreck shouldn't be. The card does what it
>does. If the rules said something like "...out-of-turn cards are played
>to defend yourself when it is not your turn," then you might have a
>point.

The (corrected) rules say you cannot use out-of-turn cards during your turn.

>    I just read Beth on the mailing list supporting the way I think
>it should be done. The question was, "what happens if both vampires
>play Majesty?" and her answer was she felt both would have a chance
>to untap.

This is incorrect.  When a "combat ends" strike is played, combat ends
right then and there, and wouldn't even progress long enough to let the
other minion declare a strike.  So it's impossible to play two Majesties
in the same combat.

(At least, that's how I was taught, and how the rules read IMHO.  I will
double check that.)

>    It even _should_ be this way. Picking your strike first can be a
>big disadvantage. This shouldn't become an advantage in the case of
>Majesty.

If choosing strike first should never be an advantage, then what about
Blood Rage?  After all, it lets the other minion know not to waste its
time striking with a weapon.

Messages.Author: Owen P Reynolds
Messages.Body:
Arrrggg!!!! I want to know where this stuff about Rotschreck
affecting the vampire _with_ claws comes from and hear it explained
wrt the card! But I'll respond to this instead.

>Sorry, but wrong.  An out-of-turn card would only be usable during your
>turn if it explicitly said it could be.
>Rotschreck is an out-of-turn card, and doesn't say it
>can be used during your turn, so can't be used during your turn.

    Well, suppose an out-of-turn card said "Play when your acting
minion... ."? It doesn't say "May be played on your turn," but we
can infer it's meant to be played on your turn. Inference _is_ a
part of figuring out how cards work.
    The question is, how useless does a card have to be "as written"
before you play by what 90% of people think was meant? Rotschreck isn't
useless, but is much less useful.

>The (corrected) rules say you cannot use out-of-turn cards during your turn.

    The corrected rules also say that any Methuselah _except_ the one
calling a vote can use Political Action cards for an extra vote. This
was just bad phrasing, and the "not on your turn" rule looks like even
worse wording. From the corrected rules:

---------
Master cards ... fall under the following subcategories:
   ...
    Locations: Location cards give your vampires certain long-term
advantages in play. ...
    Skills: Skill cards are played on your vampires. ...
    Out-of-turn: Out-of-turn cards you play when it is not your turn;
however, if you play an ... 
   ...
    Other master cards: Any master cards not explained here have their
effects explained on them.
---------

    I've written things this sloppy, but I've always had time to
reread it, realize how bad it was, and fix it. The first sentence
under locations is totally useless. No one is going to read it as a
rule (for example, Backways give a Gangrel a +1 stealth, I think.
The "rule" about locations says they give long-term advantages, so
that Gangrel gains a permanent +1 stealth when Backways is used on
them.)
    The paragraph about 'Other master cards' was only written because
they initially promised to list all the subcategories of master cards.
For 'Out-of-turn' they wanted to start with a sentence "Out of turn
cards... " that described them, the same as locations.
    It's not a rule -- it's just a product of no time to edit.

    I'm still curious why there were corrected rules even before
most people even saw the game.

>>    I just read Beth on the mailing list supporting the way I think
>>it should be done. The question was, "what happens if both vampires
>>play Majesty?" and her answer was she felt both would have a chance
>>to untap.

>This is incorrect.

    Beth really wrote it. She also said it was just her opinion, as well.

>When a "combat ends" strike is played, combat ends
>right then and there, and wouldn't even progress long enough to let the
>other minion declare a strike.  So it's impossible to play two Majesties
>in the same combat.

    The only real reference I find is in 15.3 under 'Combat Ends:'
It say that "...this ends combat immediately (before any damage is
dealt or any strike's effects take place)." The part in parenthesis
looks like it says what they mean by 'immediately'.
    I had hoped to find a clarification that emphasized the 'choose'
part of choose strike, but that section freely switches the idea of
using and selecting a strike (which we know aren't the same in the
case of normal strikes.)

>>    It even _should_ be this way. Picking your strike first can be a
>>big disadvantage. This shouldn't become an advantage in the case of
>>Majesty.

>If choosing strike first should never be an advantage, then what about
>Blood Rage?  After all, it lets the other minion know not to waste its
>time striking with a weapon.

    Right -- suppose you have a Chainsaw and I have Blood Rage. If I
go first, you punch me for a point of damage. If I go last, you try
to use your Chainsaw but Blood Rage negates the strike and I take no
damage.
    Going first was worse, so was a disadvantage.
--

much rather save it until after the opponent has played a mega-damage

think, does she have Wolf/Claws/of the Dead or not? Do I bail or sweat

OR> You're just giving your opinion and not even trying to back it up.

I've discovered that opinions do not need back up. That was, in fact,
a prediction, not a statement of known fact. You will find that 
restrictions tend to be additive until an explicit statement of

This becomes a very powerful card, indeed...

    Ah...since you are too stupid to see a use for a card even after I
post the uses for it, it should be played the exact opposite as its written.
For any other slow folks, this is how you use Rotschreck:

    Block with one of your vampires who can do aggravated damage. If
they can get to close range, consider playing Rotschreck to tap the
defender an extra turn and save yourself from a point of damage. Not great,
but good.
    If they have Fortitude or a bulletproof vest, play Rotschreck to send
them to torpor anyway. If they play a dangerous strike card or have a
good weapon, play Rotschreck to cancel it and send them to torpor. If
the play a dodge or Majesty, play Rotschreck to ignore it.
    In the latter case, there is no ruling, but Beth and Tom disagree
about how it works, so flip a coin beforehand.


>      the current asinine contention that 'Out-of-Turn' was
>  meant to read 'Out-of-Phase' aside.

    Illiterate slobs aside, anyone can see that "Out-of-turn cards you
play when it is not your turn," is telling you when you _can_ play
out-of-turn cards, not when you can't.
    It would have included a "not" or an "only," otherwise. Since it's
not a sentence in the first place, we're all just guessing, anyway.

    Why don't you review the "rule" that the Methuselah calling the
vote can't use Pol Act cards for extra votes, in light of the rulebook
and rulings, and then try and defend not allowing out-of-turn cards
on your turn.

     True, I can see that, especially if they have that annoying Kevlar
 vest on... I suppose it really depends how much you value your Master
 phase... I tend to stick in as few OoT masters as I can because I per-
 sonally hate skipping it.

    Sorry to make you repeat; but heck, I've had to repeat my own arguments
 on the other side of Rotschrek many a time... I sympathize with the annoy-
 ance it can cause...

>>      the current asinine contention that 'Out-of-Turn' was
>>  meant to read 'Out-of-Phase' aside.
>
>    Illiterate slobs aside, anyone can see that "Out-of-turn cards you
>play when it is not your turn," is telling you when you _can_ play
>out-of-turn cards, not when you can't.

     Here's where I start disagreeing with you. You're not only excluding
 the possibility of a "can't" but inserting a "can". Yes, it doesn't say
 "you only play when...", but it also doesn't say "you can play when..."
 In this case the sentence could be interpreted either as a can, telling
 you times when you can use it, or a can't, specifying times it's illegal,
 or both. I tend to think the third, since I feel it would've been called
 an Out-of-Phase master if you could play it any time other than your
 master phase. As you have it defined right now these cards suddenly become
 'play at any time' because the only time they couldn't be played would
 be during the master phase, which in most instances wouldn't matter since
 OoT's generally affect minions and such. I truly truly feel the intent
 here was to say you can't use these cards on your turn, and in fact neither
 I nor anyone I play with ever had any confusion on the sentence, grammatical
 or no. It says you play them when it's not your turn. Ergo, if it's my   
 turn, then I can't. If it's not, then I can. 

>    Why don't you review the "rule" that the Methuselah calling the
>vote can't use Pol Act cards for extra votes, in light of the rulebook
>and rulings, and then try and defend not allowing out-of-turn cards
>on your turn.

    We never had any problems with this, since it's directly contradicted
 elsewhere in the rules and so we chose the version that made more sense.
 At least, I think that's what happened... regardless, it never became an
 issue...

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
CurtAdams <curtadams@aol.com> wrote:
>>When a "combat ends" strike is played, combat ends
>>right then and there, and wouldn't even progress long enough to let the
>>other minion declare a strike.  So it's impossible to play two Majesties
>>in the same combat.
>Does this apply to Elysium, a non-strike combat ends?  I was in combat
>with someone with Elysium and wanted to play a Trap card (to get rid of
>the card.  I was expecting Elysium and needed some intercept).  Do I get
>to play my trap if and only if I can physically fling the card faster than
>he can turn his Elysium sideways?

There has been no ruling yet on "slap" conditions such as this, but
the answer will probably be something like:  acting player gets to use
action modifiers, then blocking minion, then everyone else.  Look for design
team rulings on the subject.

 mently opposed to your interpretation as you are to theirs. For my own
